title: Comparison, Choices & Envy
subtitle: Social media, social pressure and envy

slides.title: The Comparison Illusion
slides.question: Are we comparing our real lives to a fake reality?
slides.summary: An influencer posts beautiful photos of her home, dinners and weekends. Her followers assume her life is nearly perfect, but they don't see the staged photos, the money worries or the hard work behind the scenes.

expressions.meaning: show a version of your life that is selected and edited to look good.
make people believe something that isn't true.
believe something exactly as it looks, without questioning it.
make you see things in a way that isn't accurate.

items.question: Why do the influencer's followers think her life is perfect?
items.explain: "The highlights" are the best moments. A "staged" photo is planned to look natural.

items.question: What is the main message of this slide?
If you know that social media posts are carefully selected, why might they still influence your perception of other people's lives?
blocks: and distort our perception of reality.
items.explain: "So often that…" shows a result. "Distort" means to change something so it's no longer accurate.

items.question: Is presenting an idealized version of yourself online a form of dishonesty, or is it simply a matter of privacy?
blocks: showing only the highlights is privacy,
items.explain: "In my view" introduces your opinion. "But" sets the limit between the two ideas.

items.question: How can you distinguish between a genuinely successful life and a convincing public image?
blocks: reveals only part of the story.
items.explain: "I'd look at…" is a simple way to suggest a method. Remember: don't take a post at face value.

slides.title: Are You Choosing for Yourself?
slides.question: How much are your decisions really yours — and how much are they influenced by others?
slides.summary: Sarah has always liked a simple life. When her friends start buying luxury brands, she starts spending too — not because she wants to, but because she's afraid of looking less successful. Months later, she has less money and a lifestyle that doesn't suit her.

expressions.meaning: do something because others expect it, not because you want to.

expressions.en: lose sight of your own priorities
expressions.meaning: forget what really matters to you.
need approval from other people to feel good about yourself.
choose things to look good, not because they are right for you.

expressions.en: measure success on your own terms
expressions.meaning: judge success by your own values, not other people's.

items.question: Why did Sarah change her lifestyle?
items.explain: "Fit in" means to feel accepted by a group.

items.question: What was the result for Sarah?
items.explain: "Suit someone" means to be right for that person.

items.question: At what point did Sarah stop making decisions based on her own values? What might have triggered the change?
blocks: She gave in to social pressure
and lost sight of her priorities.
items.explain: "Give in to" means to stop resisting. "Lose sight of" means to forget what is important.

items.question: Is it possible to enjoy luxury and still be influenced by social pressure? How can you tell the difference?
items.explain: A simple test. If the answer is no, you're probably seeking external validation.

items.question: Should people care about how others perceive their lifestyle, or should personal satisfaction come first? Defend your position.
blocks: so I try to measure success
items.explain: "I'd argue that…" makes your position clear. "On your own terms" = by your own rules.

slides.title: Is Envy Always a Bad Thing?
slides.question: Can envy be a destructive emotion — or can it sometimes push us forward?
slides.summary: Envy can be destructive: you feel resentful of someone's success, question your own abilities or secretly hope they fail. But it can also be motivating: someone's achievements show you what you want and encourage you to take action.

expressions.meaning: use the feeling of wanting what others have as a push to act.
feel that someone's success is a danger to you.
accept and admit what makes you feel insecure.

expressions.en: channel your energy into something productive
expressions.meaning: use your energy for something useful.
use someone's example to motivate you.

items.question: What is destructive envy?
items.explain: "Resentful of" means feeling angry because something seems unfair.

items.question: What is motivating envy?
items.explain: Notice the structure: encourage someone TO do something.

items.question: Can envy be useful if it reveals something you genuinely want? Or does it always damage your peace of mind?
blocks: I think envy can be useful
if you turn it into motivation
items.explain: "Instead of" is followed by the -ING form: instead of letting.

items.question: Imagine your friend gets an opportunity you've wanted for years. What would your first reaction be, and how would you handle it?
blocks: I might feel a bit threatened,
items.explain: Use "would" ('d) and "might" for imaginary situations. Notice: inspiration FROM.

items.question: Is it better to avoid people who trigger your insecurities, or learn to deal with those feelings? Defend your answer.
blocks: and learn to deal with them,
items.explain: "Learn to deal with" = learn how to handle something. Avoiding people doesn't solve the feeling.
